items.summary: The U.S. Court of International Trade sustained in part and remanded in part Commerce's remand redetermination of the countervailing duty order on multilayered wood flooring from China, addressing Commerce's methodology for calculating the plywood benchmark price and application of adverse facts available.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of International Trade remanded the Department of Commerce's countervailing duty final determination on corrosion-resistant steel products from South Korea, finding that Commerce lacked sufficient explanation for departing from its established practice of not reexamining the countervailability of equity infusions absent new information. The court identified issues with Commerce's treatment of debt-to-equity restructurings and calculations of certain benchmark rates used to measure subsidy benefits.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit reversed a district court's dismissal of Beverly Mowry's Federal Tort Claims Act wrongful death claim. The case involved a USPS truck that struck and severely injured David Mowry; the Mowrys had previously won a judgment for his personal injuries, but the district court dismissed Beverly's subsequent wrongful death suit as barred by res judicata. The appellate court held that under Ohio law, wrongful death is an independent cause of action that accrues only upon the victim's death and therefore could not have been litigated in the prior action.

items.summary: Burton, an African-American nurse at Centre College, appealed dismissal of her retaliation and constructive discharge claims under 42 U.S.C. § 1981 after she asked about implicit bias training and raised concerns about racial discrimination. items.summary: The executive order directs the Secretary of Commerce and US Trade Representative to negotiate with foreign trading partners to adjust wind turbine imports. The Secretary's national security investigation found that wind turbines are intermittent energy sources, that foreign-produced components contain cybersecurity vulnerabilities enabling remote access, and that wind turbine operations create radar interference affecting air traffic control and military systems. The order requires negotiation progress updates within 180 days.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–122: To amend the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 to make improvements to that Act, and for other purposes. Public Law 122 Public Law 119–122 140 Stat. 1069 2026-10-15 2026-10-15 United States Government Publis
items.summary: Public Law 119-122, enacted October 15, 2026, amends the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010. The law restructures provisions related to municipal and rural infrastructure projects, repeals Section 406 of the original settlement act, and establishes an MR&I Projects Account within the Crow Settlement Fund. The legislation also extends the authorization period for Yellowtail Dam from 15 to 20 years and clarifies that the Crow Tribe retains title to and control over infrastructure constructed with settlement funds.
items.title: Public Law 119–122: To amend the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 to make improvements to that Act, and for other purposes.

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model CF34-8C1, CF34-8C5, CF34-8C5A1, CF34-8C5A2, CF34-8C5B1, CF34-8E2, CF34-8E2A1, CF34-8E5, CF34-8E5A1, CF34-8E5A2, CF34-8E5A2HA, CF34-8E6, and CF34-8E6A1 engines. This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight “Engine Degraded” messages from the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) due to corrosion of the variable geometry (VG) system actuator. This AD requires removing certain electronic engine control (EEC) full authority digital electronic control (FADEC) software versions from service and installing an updated EEC FADEC software that is eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 147 [EPA-HQ-OW-2026-0496; FRL 13209-01-OW] Utah Underground Injection Control Program; Class VI Primacy AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). ACTION: Proposed rule; notice of public heari
items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) has received a complete Underground Injection Control (UIC) program revision application from the State of Utah, requesting primary enforcement responsibility (primacy) for Class VI injection wells under Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) section 1422. The EPA's approval of the State's UIC program revision application would allow the Utah Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil, Gas and Mining (DOGM) to issue and enforce compliance with UIC Class VI permits for injection wells used for geologic carbon sequestration. In this action, the EPA proposes to approve Utah's application to implement the UIC program for Class VI injection wells located within the State, except those on Indian lands for which the EPA retains primacy. The EPA has determined that Utah's UIC Class VI program meets Federal requirements for primacy under SDWA section 1422 and the applicable implementing regulations in 40 CFR parts 144, 145, and 146.
items.title: Utah Underground Injection Control Program; Class VI Primacy
